<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=center><B>PART I</B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507922803"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937486"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937682"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937865"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306375"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306457"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306605"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306666"></A><A NAME="_Toc1542915"></A><A NAME="_Toc35422464"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 1.</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B><I>Business</I></B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937487"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937683"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937866"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516188"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306376"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>General</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>EGL, Inc. is a leading global transportation, supply chain management and information services company dedicated to providing flexible logistics solutions on a price competitive basis. &nbsp;Our services include air and ocean freight forwarding, customs brokerage, local pick up and delivery service, materials management, warehousing, trade facilitation and procurement and integrated logistics and supply chain management services. &nbsp;We provide value-added services in addition to those customarily provided by traditional air freight forwarders, ocean freight forwarders and customs brokers. &nbsp;These services are designed to provide global logistics solutions for customers in order to streamline their supply chain, reduce their inventories, improve their logistics information and provide them with more efficient and effective domestic and international distribution strategies in order to enhance their profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We believe we are one of the largest forwarders of domestic and international air freight based in the United States. &nbsp;We have a network of approximately 400 facilities, agents and distribution centers located in over 100 countries on six continents featuring advanced information systems designed to maximize cargo management efficiency and customer satisfaction. &nbsp;Each of our facilities is linked by a real-time, online communications tool that speeds the two-way flow of shipment data and related logistics information between origins and destinations around the world.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We trade on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the symbol &#147;EAGL&#148; and were incorporated in Texas in 1984.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Available Information</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We file annual, quarterly and current reports, proxy statements and other information with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#147;SEC&#148;). &nbsp;You may read and copy any document we file with the SEC at the SEC&#146;s public reference room at 450 Fifth Street, NW, Washington, D.C. 20549. &nbsp;Please call the SEC at 1-800-SEC-0330 for information on the public reference room. &nbsp;The SEC maintains a website that contains annual, quarterly and current reports, proxy statements and other information that issuers (including EGL, Inc.) file electronically with the SEC. &nbsp;The SEC&#146;s website is <I><U>http://www.sec.gov</U></I>.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our website is <I><U>http://www.eaglegl.com</U></I>. &nbsp;We make available free of charge through our internet site, via a link to the SEC&#146;s website, our annual reports on Form 10-K; quarterly reports on Form 10-Q; current reports on Form 8-K; and any amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;) as soon as reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with, or furnished to, the SEC. &nbsp;We also make available on our website our Corporate Governance Guidelines and information about our Board of Directors, including committee charters. &nbsp;The information on our website is not incorporated by reference into and is not a part of this report.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc510516190"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306378"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937488"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937684"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937867"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516189"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306377"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Industry Overview </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As business requirements for efficient and cost-effective distribution services have increased, so have the importance and complexity of effective supply chain management. &nbsp;Businesses increasingly strive to minimize inventory levels with just-in-time processes, perform manufacturing and assembly operations in multiple locations and distribute products to numerous destinations. &nbsp;As a result, companies frequently want expedited or time-definite deferred shipment services. &nbsp;Time-definite deferred shipments are delivered at a specific time and are typically not expedited, which results in a lower rate than for an expedited shipment.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>1</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Customers have two principal freight forwarding alternatives: &nbsp;an air freight forwarder or a fully-integrated carrier. &nbsp;An air freight forwarder procures shipments from customers and arranges transportation of the cargo on a carrier. &nbsp;An air freight forwarder may also arrange pick up from the shipper to the carrier and delivery of the shipment from the carrier to the recipient. &nbsp;Air freight forwarders often tailor shipment routing to meet the customer&#146;s price and service requirements. &nbsp;Fully-integrated carriers provide pick up and delivery service, primarily through their own captive fleets of trucks and aircraft. &nbsp;Because air freight forwarders select from various transportation options in routing customer shipments, they are often able to serve customers less expensively and with greater flexibility than integrated carriers. &nbsp;In addition to the high fixed expenses associated with owning, operating and maintaining fleets of aircraft, trucks and related equipment, integrated carriers often impose significant restrictions on delivery schedules and shipment weight, size and type. &nbsp;Air freight forwarders, however, generally handle shipments of any size and can offer a variety of customized shipping options.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Most air freight forwarders, like EGL, focus on heavier cargo and do not generally compete with integrated shippers of primarily smaller parcels, including FedEx Corporation. &nbsp;Several integrated carriers, like United Parcel Service (&#147;UPS&#148;) and Deutsche Post AG, operating under the brand name and referred to herein as &#147;DHL&#148;, do focus on shipments of heavy cargo in competition with forwarders. &nbsp;On occasion, integrated shippers serve as a source of cargo space to forwarders. &nbsp;Additionally, most air freight forwarders do not generally compete with the major commercial airlines, which, to some extent, depend on forwarders to procure shipments and supply freight to fill cargo space on their scheduled flights.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The air freight forwarding industry is highly fragmented. &nbsp;Many companies in the industry are able to meet only a portion of their customers&#146; required transportation service needs. &nbsp;Some national domestic air freight forwarders rely on networks of terminals operated by franchisees or agents. &nbsp;We believe that the development and operation of company-owned terminals and staff under the supervision of our management have enabled us to maintain a greater degree of financial and operational control and service quality than franchise-based networks.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We believe there are several factors that are increasing demand for global logistics solutions. &nbsp;These factors include:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>outsourcing of logistics functions;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>globalization of demand and supply chains; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>increased complexity of supply chains.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Our Competitive Advantages</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a global transportation, supply chain management and information services company, we believe that we are well-positioned to provide cost-effective and efficient solutions to address the demand in the marketplace for transportation and logistics services. &nbsp;We believe that the most important competitive factors in our industry are quality of service (including reliability, responsiveness, expertise and convenience), scope of operations, geographic coverage, information technology and price. &nbsp;We believe our primary competitive advantages are: &nbsp;(i) our low cost non-asset based business model; (ii) our global infrastructure; (iii) our information technology resources and (iv) our diverse customer base.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Non-asset based business model</I>. &nbsp;With relatively no dedicated or fixed transportation costs, we are able to leverage our network and offer competitive pricing and flexible solutions to our customers. &nbsp;Moreover, our balanced product offering provides us with revenue streams from multiple sources and enables us to retain customers even as they shift from priority to deferred shipments of their products. &nbsp;We believe our model allows us to provide low-cost solutions to our customers while also generating revenues from multiple modes of transportation and logistics services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>2</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Global presence with North American infrastructure</I>. &nbsp;Our global infrastructure enables us to provide a closed-loop logistics chain to our customers worldwide. &nbsp;Within North America, our infrastructure consists of our pick up and delivery network, air and ground networks, and logistics and warehousing capabilities. &nbsp;Our ground and pick up and delivery networks enable us to service the growing time-definite deferred forwarding market while providing the domestic service for international shipments once they reach North America. &nbsp;In addition, we believe our heavyweight air network provides for the lowest available costs on shipments, as we have no dedicated charters or leases and can capitalize on available capacity in the market to move our customers&#146; goods. &nbsp;Lastly, we have adequate warehouse and dock space available to leverage our North America infrastructure for future growth and/or to provide such space to our customers for their logistics needs.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Information technology resources</I>. &nbsp;A primary component of our business strategy is the continued development of advanced information systems to continually provide accurate and timely shipment information to our management and customers. &nbsp;Our customer delivery tools enable connectivity with our customers&#146; and trading partners&#146; systems, which leads to more accurate and up-to-date information on the status of shipments.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Diverse customer base</I>. &nbsp;While computers and other high-technology equipment manufacturers and retailers continue to comprise a significant portion of our customer base, our customer base has increasingly diversified into a variety of sectors including the retail, pharmaceutical and the oil and gas industries. &nbsp;As such, we continue to focus on expanding lines of business with current customers and adding new accounts in similar and new categories of shippers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a global transportation, supply chain management and information services company, our revenues are generated from a number of services, including air freight forwarding, ocean freight forwarding, customs brokerage, logistics and other services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Air Freight Forwarding and Consolidation Services</B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937493"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937689"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937872"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516191"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306379"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our air freight forwarding operations include international and domestic air freight forwarding. Our total air freight forwarding revenues in 2005 were $2.0 billion, of which 25% were derived from domestic air freight forwarding within the United States and 75% were derived from international air freight forwarding. &nbsp;Our air freight forwarding and related logistics services include the following:</P>
<A NAME="OLE_LINK1"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>domestic freight forwarding;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>international freight forwarding;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-13.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-0.2pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>inland transportation of freight from point of origin to distribution center or the carrier&#146;s cargo terminal and from our terminal in the destination city to the recipient (pick up and delivery);</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>cargo assembly;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>export packing and vendor shipment consolidation;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-13.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-0.2pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>receiving and breaking down consolidated air freight shipments and arranging for distribution of the individual shipments;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>charter arrangement and handling;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>electronic transmittal of logistics documentation;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>electronic purchase order/shipment tracking;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>3</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>expedited document delivery to overseas destinations for customs clearance; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>procurement of cargo insurance.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We neither own nor operate any aircraft and, consequently, are not limited to specific delivery schedules or shipment sizes. &nbsp;We arrange for transportation of our customers&#146; shipments via commercial airlines, air cargo carriers, third-party truck brokers, trucking companies and independent owner-operators of trucks and trailers. &nbsp;We select the carrier for a shipment based on route, service capability, available cargo capacity and cost. &nbsp;We charter cargo aircraft from time to time depending upon seasonality, freight volumes and other factors.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We generate air freight forwarding revenues by acting primarily as an indirect air carrier and, to a lesser extent, as an authorized cargo sales agent. &nbsp;As an indirect air carrier, we obtain shipments from our customers, consolidate shipments bound for a particular destination, determine the best means to transport the shipment to its destination, select the direct carrier (an airline) on which the consolidated lot is to move and tender each consolidated lot as a single shipment to the direct carrier for transportation to a destination. &nbsp;At the destination, we or our agent receive the consolidated lot, break it into its component shipments and distribute the individual shipments to the consignees.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our rates are based on a charge per pound/kilogram. &nbsp;We ordinarily charge the shipper a rate less than the rate that the shipper would be charged if they went directly to an airline. &nbsp;Due to the high volume of freight we manage, we generally obtain lower rates per pound/kilogram from airlines than the rates we charge our customers for individual shipments. &nbsp;This rate differential is the primary source of our air freight forwarding net revenues. &nbsp;Our practice is to make prompt adjustments in our rates to match changes in airline rates.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As an authorized cargo sales agent of most airlines worldwide, we also arrange for the transportation of individual shipments and receive a commission from the airline for arranging the shipments. &nbsp;In addition, we provide the shipper with ancillary services, such as export documentation, for which we receive a separate fee. &nbsp;When acting in this capacity, we do not consolidate shipments or have responsibility for shipments once they have been tendered to the airline. &nbsp;We conduct our agency air freight forwarding operations from the same facilities as our indirect carrier operations and serve the same regions of the world.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Local transportation services are performed either by independent cartage companies or, in the United States and Canada, primarily by our local pick up and delivery operations. &nbsp;See Domestic Local Delivery Services. &nbsp;If delivery schedules permit, we will typically use lower-cost, overland truck transportation services, including those obtained through our domestic truck brokerage operations. &nbsp;See Domestic Truck Brokerage Services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We draw on our logistical expertise to provide forwarding services that are tailored to meet customer needs and, in addition to regularly scheduled service, we offer customized schedules. &nbsp;Our services are customized to address each client&#146;s individual shipping requirements, generally without restrictions on shipment weight, size or type. &nbsp;Once the customer&#146;s requirements for an individual shipment have been established, we proactively manage the execution of the shipment to ensure satisfaction of the customer&#146;s requirements.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our air freight forwarding business is not dependent on any one customer or industry. &nbsp;We provide services to global or multinational customers as well as regional customers. &nbsp;In 2005, approximately 59% of our net revenues were attributable to air freight forwarding.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:10pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We have an ongoing relationship with DHL in which DHL provides us capacity in their North American air system. &nbsp;This provides broad coverage into key markets.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>4</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Domestic local delivery services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In the United States and Canada, we provide same-day local pick up and delivery services, both for shipments where we are acting as an air freight forwarder as well as for third-party customers requiring pick up and delivery within the same metropolitan area. &nbsp;We believe that these services provide an important complement to our air freight forwarding services by allowing for quality control over the critical pick up and delivery segments of the transportation process as well as allowing for prompt, updated information on the status of a customer&#146;s shipment at each step in the shipment process. &nbsp;We focus on providing local pick up and delivery services to customers with a relatively high volume of business, which we believe provides a greater potential for profitability than a broader base of small, infrequent customers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As of December 31, 2005, local delivery services were offered in 77 of the 88 cities in the United States and Canada in which our terminals were located. &nbsp;In all other cities, we have arrangements with agents to handle pick up and delivery services. &nbsp;On-demand pick up and delivery services are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. &nbsp;In most locations, delivery drivers are independent contractors who operate their own vehicles. &nbsp;Our Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee and Atlanta, Georgia operations include a number of company-owned or leased trailers, trucks and other ground equipment primarily to service specific customer accounts.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Local pick up and delivery revenues were $334.8 million during 2005 and $289.8 million during 2004. &nbsp;Approximately $188.3 million of these revenues during 2005 and $166.7 million of these revenues during 2004 were attributable to our air freight forwarding operations and were eliminated upon consolidation. &nbsp;The remaining pick up and delivery revenues were attributable to local delivery services for third-party, non-forwarding business. &nbsp;A substantial majority of the total cost of providing for local pick up and delivery of our freight forwarding shipments in 2005 and 2004 was attributable to our own local pick up and delivery services. &nbsp;Revenues from domestic local delivery services, net of intercompany revenues, are included in air freight forwarding revenues.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937494"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937690"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937873"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516192"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306380"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Domestic truck brokerage services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We have established truck brokerage operations in the United States, Europe and China to provide logistical support to our forwarding operations and, to a lesser extent, to provide truckload service to selected customers. &nbsp;In the United States, our truck brokerage operations operate under the Select Carrier Group (SCG) name. &nbsp;Our truck brokerage services locate and secure capacity when overland transportation is the most efficient means of meeting customer delivery requirements, especially in cases of air freight customers choosing the deferred delivery option. &nbsp;We use internal truck brokerage operations to meet delivery requirements without having to rely on third-party truck brokerage services. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Additionally, by providing for our own truck brokerage, we have been able to achieve greater efficiencies and utilize purchasing power over transportation providers. &nbsp;We do not own a significant number of the trucks used in our truck brokerage operations and, instead, primarily use carriers or independent owner-operators of ground capacity on an as-needed basis. &nbsp;We use our relationships with a number of independent trucking companies to obtain truck and trailer space.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As with local pick up and delivery services, we view our truck brokerage services primarily as a means of maintaining quality control and enhancing customer service of our core air freight forwarding business, as well as a means of capturing a portion of profits that would otherwise be earned by third parties. &nbsp;Revenues from domestic truck brokerage, net of intercompany revenues, are included in air freight forwarding revenues.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>International Ocean Freight Forwarding and Consolidation</B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937502"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937698"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937881"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516195"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306383"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a global ocean freight forwarder, we arrange for the shipment of freight by ocean carriers and act as the agent of the shipper or the importer. &nbsp;Our ocean freight forwarding and related logistics services include inland transportation from point of origin to distribution facility or port of export, cargo assembly, packing and consolidation, warehousing, electronic transmittal of documentation and shipment tracking, expedited document delivery, pre-alert consignee notification and cargo insurance.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>A number of our facilities provide protective cargo packing, crating and specialized handling services for retail goods, government-specification cargo, consumer goods, hazardous cargo, heavy machinery and assemblies and perishable cargo. &nbsp;Other facilities are equipped to handle equipment and material from multiple origins to overseas &#147;turn-key&#148; projects, such as manufacturing facilities or government installations. &nbsp;We do not own or operate ships or assume carrier responsibility, preferring to retain the flexibility to tailor logistics, services and options to customer requirements.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our compensation for ocean freight forwarding services is derived principally from commissions paid by shipping lines and from forwarding and documentation fees paid by customers, who are either shippers or consignees. &nbsp;In 2005, approximately 3% of our net revenues were attributable to international ocean freight forwarding, including commissions, forwarding fees and associated ancillary services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our global operations as an indirect ocean carrier or NVOCC (non-vessel operating common carrier) are similar in some respects to our air freight consolidation operations. &nbsp;We procure customer freight, consolidate shipments bound for a particular destination, determine the routing, select the ocean carrier or charter a ship and tender each consolidated lot as a single shipment to the direct carrier for transportation to a distribution point. &nbsp;As a NVOCC, we generally derive our revenues from the spread between the rate charged to our customer and the ocean carrier&#146;s charge to us for carrying the shipment, in addition to charging for other ancillary services related to the movement of the freight. &nbsp;Because of the volume of freight we control and consolidate, we are generally able to obtain lower rates from ocean carriers than the rate the shipper would be able to procure going directly to the carrier. &nbsp;In 2005, ocean freight consolidation and associated ancillary services contributed approximately 6% of our net revenues.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a third party logistics provider (3PL), we assist our customers in the management and fulfillment of their purchase orders down to the part or stock keeping unit (sku) level. &nbsp;We work closely with our customer&#146;s suppliers to coordinate and arrange for the movement of the goods from the manufacturing line to the ports and ultimately to the destination distribution center or directly to their customers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Customs Brokerage </B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937503"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937699"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937882"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516196"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306384"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We function as a customs broker at approximately 50 locations in the United States and in over 300 international locations through our network of offices and agents. &nbsp;In our capacity as a customs broker, we prepare and file all formal documentation required for clearance through customs agencies, obtain customs bonds, in many cases facilitate the payment of import duties on behalf of the importer, arrange for payment of collect freight charges and assist the importer in obtaining the most appropriate commodity classifications and in qualifying for duty drawback refunds. &nbsp;Our customs brokers and support staff have substantial knowledge of the complex tariff laws and customs regulations governing the payment of duty, as well as valuation and import restrictions in their respective countries. &nbsp;Within the United States, we employ a significant number of personnel holding individual customs broker licenses.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We rely both on company-designed and third-party computer technology for customs brokerage activities performed on behalf of our clients. &nbsp;We utilize the Automated Broker Interface information system, providing an online link with the Bureau of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). &nbsp;In several global trading centers, in addition to the United States, our offices are connected electronically to customs agencies for expedited pre-clearance of goods and centralized import management. &nbsp;Such online </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>interface with customs agencies speeds freight release and provides nationwide control of clearances at multiple ports and airports of entry.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We work with importers to design cost-effective import programs that utilize our distribution and logistics services and computer technology. &nbsp;Such services include:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>electronic document preparation;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>cargo routing from overseas origins to ports and airports of entry;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>foreign trade zone utilization;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>bonded warehousing;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>distribution of the cleared cargo to inland locations; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>trade compliance consulting.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In many United States and overseas locations, our bonded warehouses enable importers to defer payment of customs duties and coordinate release of cargo with their production or distribution schedules. &nbsp;Goods are stored under customs service supervision until the importer is ready to withdraw or re-export them. &nbsp;We receive storage charges for these in-transit goods and fees for related ancillary services. &nbsp;We also offer Foreign Trade Zone management and trade compliance consulting services to provide customers with additional tools to maintain cost-effective compliant import programs.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a customs broker operating in the United States, we are licensed by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and regulated by the CBP. &nbsp;Our fees for acting as a customs broker in the United States are not regulated, and we do not have a fixed fee schedule for customs brokerage services. &nbsp;Instead, fees are generally based on the volume of business transacted for a particular customer, and the type, number and complexity of services provided. &nbsp;In addition to fees, we bill the importer for amounts that we have paid on the importer&#146;s behalf, including duties, collect freight charges and similar payments. &nbsp;In 2005, approximately 16% of our net revenues were attributable to customs brokerage services.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We are committed to helping our customers secure their global supply chains from the global threat of terror. &nbsp;As such, we have actively engaged in all U.S. government initiatives in the post September 2001 market. &nbsp;We are a validated participant in the Customs - Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) and a member of the Business Anti-Smuggling Coalition (BASC). &nbsp;We meet the requirements of the Trade Act of 2002 and, pursuant to regulations established by the U.S. CBP, transmit advanced shipment information for all U.S. import and transit shipments regardless of mode of transport. &nbsp;Further, we continually review and update our processes and procedures to ensure compliance with all new government agency requirements, such as the record keeping requirements related to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration&#146;s implementation of the Bio Terrorism Act. &nbsp;We are also preparing for similar supply chain security initiatives in other jurisdictions outside of the U.S. that we believe will be the outgrowth of the World Customs Organization&#146;s Framework of Standards. &nbsp;As a result, we believe our customs brokerage strengths include the following:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>over 100 years of experience in importing goods into the United States;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>ISO certified desk level processes for consistency and compliance;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>infrastructure of licensed professionals;</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Customs-Trade Partners Against Terrorism, or C-TPAT, partner engaged in supply chain security; and</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Logistics and Other Services </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Customers increasingly demand more than the movement of freight from their transportation suppliers. &nbsp;To meet these needs, suppliers seek to extend the services offered by their logistics partners, by, among other things, providing information on the status of materials, components and finished goods throughout the logistics supply chain and service performance reports on and proof of delivery for each shipment. &nbsp;They also look for the physical distribution expertise associated with the physical distribution and warehouse management of their valuable merchandise. &nbsp;We provide a range of logistics services, distribution and materials management services, international insurance services, global project management services and trade facilitation services. &nbsp;In 2005, approximately 16% of our net revenues were attributable to logistics and other services.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937504"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937700"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937883"></A><A NAME="_Toc508123061"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Logistics services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We use our logistics expertise to maximize the efficiency and performance of our customers&#146; supply chains by providing solutions tailored to their specific needs. &nbsp;We provide logistics services to our clients that are transactional or commodity based, have pricing models that are contractual (fixed or variable) where we focus mainly on reducing our customers&#146; cost structure and providing specialized services (e.g., order processing, product configuration). &nbsp;In addition, we provide transportation consulting services and make our expertise and resources available to assist customers in balancing their transportation needs against budgetary constraints by developing logistics plans. &nbsp;We staff and manage the shipping departments of some of our customers that outsource their transportation management function. &nbsp;We also provide other ancillary services, including electronic data interchange, customized shipping reports, computerized tracking of shipments, air and ocean charters, cargo assembly and protective packing and crating.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937505"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937701"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937884"></A><A NAME="_Toc508123062"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Distribution and materials management services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We offer a wide range of customized inbound logistics and distribution management of our customers&#146; inventory. &nbsp;We often provide these materials management services in conjunction with the transportation of cargo. &nbsp;These services are provided in a number of our owned and leased logistics facilities in many locations throughout the world. &nbsp;During 2005, we continued our program of improving existing facilities to meet customer needs. &nbsp;Our distribution and materials management services include inventory control, vendor managed inventory (VMI) services, order processing, import and export freight staging, protective and specialized packing and crating, pick-and-pack operations, containerization, consolidation and deconsolidation and special handling for perishables, hazardous materials and heavy-lift equipment. &nbsp;For import shipments, we provide bonded warehouse services and, in certain locations, Free Trade Zone services. &nbsp;These warehouse and distribution services complement our other transportation services, including the information systems tools that are the enabler of the integrated logistics solutions we offer to customers.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937508"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937704"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937887"></A><A NAME="_Toc508123065"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Trade facilitation services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We provide procurement, financial and distribution management services to certain multinational customers. &nbsp;We purchase both raw materials for manufacturing and finished goods for distribution, then coordinate their global deployment, as directed by the customer. &nbsp;We deliver services through custom-designed Vendor and Distribution Hub programs. &nbsp;We are able to coordinate a customer&#146;s procurement, logistics, transportation and distribution activities within a single supply chain program. &nbsp;This enables us to optimize customer supply chains by streamlining the material, information and financial flows through integration of the specific supply chain processes and elimination of redundant transactions.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Insurance</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We arrange international insurance for our customers in connection with our air freight and ocean freight forwarding operations. &nbsp;Insurance coverage is frequently tailored to a customer&#146;s shipping program and is procured for the customer as a component of our integrated logistics. &nbsp;We also arrange for surety bonds for importers as part of our customs brokerage activities. &nbsp;We report insurance revenues in air freight forwarding, ocean freight forwarding or customs brokerage and other revenues based on the nature of the insured shipment.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937509"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937705"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937888"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516198"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306386"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937495"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937691"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937874"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516197"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306385"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Information Systems</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>A primary component of our business strategy is the continued development of advanced information systems. &nbsp;We have invested substantial management and financial resources in the development of our information systems in an effort to provide accurate and timely information to our management and customers. &nbsp;We believe that our systems have been instrumental in the productivity of our personnel, tracking of revenues and costs and the quality of our operations and service, and have resulted in substantial reductions in paperwork, and expedited the entry, processing, retrieval and internal dissemination of critical information. &nbsp;These systems also enable us to provide customers with accurate and up-to-date information on the status of their shipments through a wide range of media, which has become increasingly important.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We continue to expand our product offering to provide air, ocean and ground transportation services, warehousing and inventory management, customs and purchase order processing. &nbsp;Each of the services is supported by specific computer applications that facilitate the operational processes. &nbsp;In addition, we image many of the documents to support proof of delivery, compliance and retention.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We continue to invest in our information systems technology in order to provide a flexible, scalable information system environment that provides a seamless flow of data across the globe, improves our ability to manage customer expectations, and increases operational efficiencies throughout our organization. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We have organized our computer applications to support the supply chain process. &nbsp;These applications are grouped into four broad categories as follows:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Transportation Management Systems, which include our traditional freight forwarding and consolidation systems, our pick up and delivery systems for dispatching our owner operated vehicles and route optimization systems for our dedicated fleet of vehicles.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Regulatory Management Systems, which support our export and import processing. &nbsp;These are country specific to comply with local regulatory and reporting requirements.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Material Management Systems, for our logistics, warehouse management and distribution operations.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Financial Management Systems, for our global accounting, intercompany settlement, receivables and payable management, consolidation, and internal and external financial reporting.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Some of these applications are linked together through our data repositories or data warehouse to enable us to deliver information and provide visibility both internally and externally.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Currently our Information Technology strategic initiatives include:</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>upgrading our financial management, human resources and international operational systems on a global basis; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>continuing to expand our business connectivity with our customers&#146; systems. &nbsp;This includes, but is not limited to, receiving shipment requests, advance shipment notices, commercial invoices and other data electronically from our customers and providing status information electronically back to our customers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Sales and Marketing </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We market services and supply chain solutions through a global sales organization of nearly 550 full-time sales people. &nbsp;Our sales organization continues to be one of our differentiating factors in the marketplace. &nbsp;All of our leaders, from senior management down to the station managers, support our sales people with an active and targeted selling approach. &nbsp;Our managers at each station are responsible for customer service and the daily execution of customer requirements focusing on a level of service that we believe will exceed customer expectations. &nbsp;This includes proactively managing existing customer requirements for accounts with national and global scope as well as coordinating and communicating requirements for local customers or national/global account affiliates. &nbsp;Our station managers are responsible for the overall results of their facility and are empowered to make decisions to support our customers and return a fair profit. &nbsp;In addition, our divisional and regional managers are responsible for the financial performance of the assigned stations within their division or region. &nbsp;Our employees are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week to respond to our customers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Customer retention and strengthening current relationships to participate in new business opportunities is important to us, and we emphasize this throughout our organization. &nbsp;Our logistics or &#147;non-transportation&#148; revenues continues to be a critical part of our revenue base and we will continue to market, design and execute supply chain solutions aimed at reducing our customer&#146;s delivery costs and strengthening our customer alliances. &nbsp;We continue to emphasize the development of national and global accounts while aggressively targeting local accounts where we can leverage our array of services and North America network. &nbsp;The larger, more complex accounts typically have many requirements ranging from very detailed standard operating procedures on international opportunities to customized information technology requirements. &nbsp;Our global network allows us to provide one-stop shopping solutions for these multi-national organizations. &nbsp;We believe our recent growth and cost optimization has enabled us to more effectively compete for and obtain many new accounts.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Customers </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our customers are manufacturers and distributors of a vast array of goods in many different industries including, but not limited to, electronic and high-technology, automotive, oil and gas, energy, retail, pharmaceutical and health care, machinery, printed matter, trade show materials and aerospace. &nbsp;We also continue to expand our business with government agencies and defense entities globally. &nbsp;In 2005, no customer accounted for more than 5% of our revenues. &nbsp;Despite this healthy diversification of customers, adverse conditions in some of our larger business sectors could have an impact on our </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>10</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>business should there be a significant decrease in our customers&#146; volumes. &nbsp;We expect that demand for our services, and consequently results of operations will continue to be sensitive to domestic and global economic conditions and other factors we cannot directly control. &nbsp;As such, our focus will remain on expanding lines of business with current customers and adding new accounts through our field and global sales teams.</P>

<A NAME="_Toc507937511"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937707"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937890"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516199"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306387"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Regulation</B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937510"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937706"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937889"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516200"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306388"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Failure to comply with the applicable regulations or to maintain required permits or licenses could result in substantial fines or revocation of our permits or authorities. &nbsp;We cannot give assurance as to the degree or cost of future regulations on our business. &nbsp;Some of the regulations affecting our operations are described below.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Air freight forwarding</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our business is subject to regulation as an indirect air cargo carrier under the Federal Aviation Act by the U.S. Department of Transportation, although air freight forwarders are exempted from most of the Federal Aviation Act&#146;s requirements by the Economic Aviation Regulations. &nbsp;We are also regulated by the Transportation Security Administration and the Department of Homeland Security. &nbsp;Our foreign air freight forwarding operations are subject to similar regulation by the regulatory authorities of the respective foreign jurisdictions. &nbsp;The air freight forwarding industry is subject to regulatory and legislative changes that can affect the economics of the industry by requiring changes in operating practices or influencing the demand for, and the costs of providing, services to customers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Domestic local delivery services and domestic truck brokerage services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our delivery operations are subject to various state and local regulations and, in many instances, require permits and licenses from state authorities. &nbsp;In addition, some of our delivery operations are regulated by the Surface Transportation Board of the U.S. Department of Transportation. &nbsp;These federal, state and local authorities have broad powers, including the power to approve specified mergers, consolidations and acquisitions and to regulate the delivery of some types of shipments and operations </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>11</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>within particular geographic areas. &nbsp;The Surface Transportation Board has the power to regulate motor carrier operations, to approve some rates, charges and accounting systems and to require periodic financial reporting. &nbsp;Interstate motor carrier operations are also subject to safety requirements prescribed by the U.S. Department of Transportation. &nbsp;In some potential locations for our delivery operations, state and local permits and licenses may be difficult to obtain. &nbsp;Our truck brokerage operations subject us to regulation as a property broker by the Surface Transportation Board, and we have obtained a property broker license and surety bond.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Ocean freight forwarding</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Federal Maritime Commission, or FMC, regulates our ocean forwarding operations. &nbsp;The FMC licenses ocean freight forwarders. &nbsp;Indirect ocean carriers (non-vessel operating common carriers) are subject to FMC regulation, under the FMC tariff filing and surety bond requirements, and under the Shipping Act of 1984, particularly those terms proscribing rebating practices.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Customs brokerage</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our United States customs brokerage operations are subject to the licensing requirements of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and are regulated by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). &nbsp;We have received our customs brokerage license from the CBP and additional related government approvals to conduct customs business in the U.S. &nbsp;Our foreign customs brokerage operations are licensed in and subject to the regulations of their respective countries.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Security</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As security measures have increased around the globe and the United States focuses more heavily on import security, we have adopted certain measures to be well-positioned for the new U.S. government focus on security. &nbsp;The U.S. Department of Homeland Security and the CBP have certified us as a member of the C-TPAT. &nbsp;Further we were one of the first 100 members of C-TPAT to have our security procedures, standards and technology validated by CBP in 2003. &nbsp;As part of our layered approach to supply chain security, we have also been certified as a member of the Business Anti Smuggling Coalition (BASC). &nbsp;In December 2003, we began the Prior Notice reporting of human and animal food shipments as required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration BioTerrorism Act. &nbsp;Further all of our facilities have been registered with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as required by the BioTerrorism Act to ensure that we can meet the global transportation needs of our customers. &nbsp;We are also anticipating and preparing for similar security initiatives outside the U.S.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Logistics and other services</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Some portions of our warehouse operations require:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>registration under the Gambling Act of 1962 and a license or registration by the U.S. Department of Justice;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>authorizations and bonds by the U.S. Treasury;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>a license by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco &amp; Firearms of the U.S. Treasury; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>approvals by the U.S. Customs Service.</P>

<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Environmental</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In the United States, we are subject to federal, state and local provisions relating to the discharge of materials into the environment or otherwise for the protection of the environment. &nbsp;Similar laws apply in many foreign jurisdictions where we operate or may operate in the future. &nbsp;Although current operations have not been significantly affected by compliance with these environmental laws, governments are becoming increasingly sensitive to environmental issues, and we cannot predict what impact future environmental regulations may have on our business. &nbsp;We do not anticipate making any material capital expenditures for environmental control purposes.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Employees </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We had over 10,500 employees at December 31, 2005, including approximately 550 sales personnel. &nbsp;None of our employees are currently covered by a collective bargaining agreement. &nbsp;We have experienced no work stoppages and consider our relations with employees to be good. &nbsp;Our owned or leased vehicles were driven by approximately 130 of our employees as of December 31, 2005.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We pay our entire sales force and most of our operations personnel what we believe is significantly more than the industry average through the use of incentive and commission programs. &nbsp;We offer a broad-based compensation plan to these employees. &nbsp;Sales personnel are paid a gross commission based on the net revenues of shipments sold. &nbsp;Operations personnel and management are paid bonuses based on the profitability of their locations as well as on our overall profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><B>Independent contractors</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><B></B>We also had contracts with approximately 1,900 independent owner/operators of local delivery services as of December 31, 2005. &nbsp;The independent owner/operators own, operate and maintain the vehicles they use in their work for us and may employ qualified drivers of their choice.</P>

Crane</I>. &nbsp;Mr. Crane has served as our Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of Directors since he founded EGL in March 1984. &nbsp;Mr. Crane has a total of 24 years experience in the transportation industry. &nbsp;Mr. Crane is a member of the Compensation Committee and of the Governance / Nominating Committee. &nbsp;Mr. Crane is a Director of the Houston Museum of Natural Science.</P>
