<A NAME="_Toc507937535"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937731"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937914"></A><A NAME="_Toc510516203"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306391"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 1A.</B></P>
<B><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:72pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><I>Risk Factors</I></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Factors That May Affect Future Results and Financial Condition</B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507922804"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937512"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937708"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937891"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>You should read carefully the following factors and all other information contained in this report. &nbsp;If any of the risks and uncertainties described below or elsewhere in this report actually occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially adversely affected. &nbsp;In that case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and an investor may lose all or part of his investment.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:4226.585pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>We may not be successful in growing either internally or through acquisitions.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our growth strategy primarily focuses on internal growth in domestic and international freight forwarding, local pick up and delivery, customs brokerage and truck brokerage and, to a lesser extent, on acquisitions. &nbsp;Our ability to grow will depend on a number of factors, including:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>existing and emerging competition;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>ability to open new terminals;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>ability to operate profitably in the face of competitive pressures;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the recruitment, training and retention of operating and management employees;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the strength of demand for our services;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the availability of capital to support our growth; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the ability to identify, negotiate and fund acquisitions when appropriate.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Acquisitions involve risks, including those relating to:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the integration of acquired businesses, including different information systems;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the retention of prior levels of business;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the retention of employees;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the diversion of management attention;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the amortization of acquired intangible assets; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>unexpected liabilities.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We cannot assure you that we will be successful in implementing any of our business strategies or plans for future growth.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>15</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Risks associated with operating in international markets could restrict our ability to expand globally and harm our business and prospects.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We market and sell our services in the United States and internationally. &nbsp;We anticipate that international sales will continue to account for a significant portion of our total revenues for the foreseeable future. &nbsp;We presently conduct our international sales in the following geographic areas: &nbsp;North America, Europe, Asia, Middle East, India, Africa, South America and South Pacific. &nbsp;Economic conditions, including those resulting from wars, civil unrest, acts of terrorism and other conflicts may adversely affect the global economy, our customers and their ability to pay for our services. &nbsp;There are numerous risks inherent in conducting our business internationally, including:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>general political and economic instability in international markets, including heightened security measures, which could impede our ability to deliver our services to customers and adversely affect our results of operations;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>changes in regulatory requirements, which could restrict our ability to deliver services to our international customers;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>export restrictions, tariffs, licenses and other trade barriers, which could prevent us from adequately equipping our facilities worldwide;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>differing technology standards across countries, which may impede our ability to integrate our services across international borders;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>increased expenses associated with marketing services in foreign countries, which could affect our ability to compete;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>difficulties in staffing and managing foreign operations;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the imposition of additional taxes in foreign jurisdictions;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>complex foreign laws and treaties, which could adversely affect our ability to operate our business profitably; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>difficulties in collecting accounts receivable.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>These and other risks could impede our ability to manage our international operations effectively, limit the future growth of our business, increase our costs and require significant management attention.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Events impacting the volume of international trade and international operations could adversely affect our international operations.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our international operations are directly related to and dependent on the volume of international trade, particularly trade between the United States and foreign nations. &nbsp;This trade, as well as our international operations, are influenced by many factors, including:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>economic and political conditions in the United States and abroad;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>major work stoppages;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>difficulties in managing overseeing foreign operations;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>exchange controls and currency fluctuations;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>16</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>wars, civil unrest, acts of terrorism and other conflicts; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-13.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>United States and foreign laws relating to tariffs, trade restrictions, foreign investment and taxation.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Trade-related events beyond our control, such as a failure of various nations to reach or adopt international trade agreements or an increase in bilateral or multilateral trade restrictions, could have a material adverse effect on our international operations.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><I>As a U.S. government contractor, we are subject to a number of procurement and other rules and regulations.</I> </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>To do business with government agencies, either directly as a contractor or indirectly as a subcontractor, we must comply with and are affected by many laws and regulations, including those relating to the formation, administration and performance of U.S. government contracts. These laws and regulations, among other things:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>require, in some cases, certification and disclosure of all cost and pricing data in connection with contract negotiations; </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>impose accounting rules that define allowable costs and otherwise govern our right to reimbursement under certain cost-based U.S. government contracts; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.7pt; text-indent:-13.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>restrict the use and dissemination of information classified for national security purposes and the exportation of certain products and technical data.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>These laws and regulations affect how we do business with our customers and, in some instances, impose added costs on our business. A violation of these laws and regulations could result in the imposition of fines and penalties or the termination of our contracts. &nbsp;In addition, the violation of certain other generally applicable laws and regulations could result in our suspension or debarment as a government contractor.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Fuel shortages and price volatility could adversely affect our business and operations. </I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:396pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our suppliers generally pass on increases in the price of fuel to us and we generally pass these price increases on to our customers through the imposition of a surcharge.&nbsp; We sometimes bear a portion of price increases over the short-term. There can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to impose such surcharges in the future.&nbsp; In addition, if fuel costs increase significantly, our customers may reduce the volume and frequency of cargo shipments or find other less costly alternatives for cargo delivery.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The price of fuel is directly influenced by the price of crude oil and to a lesser extent by refining capacity relative to demand, which are influenced by a wide variety of macroeconomic and geopolitical events and is completely beyond our control. Additionally, hostilities in the Middle East and terrorist attacks in the U.S. and abroad could cause significant disruptions in the supply of crude oil and have had a significant impact on the price and availability of fuel. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our business is subject to seasonal trends.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Historically, our operating results have been subject to seasonal trends, when measured on a quarterly basis. &nbsp;Typically, our first fiscal quarter is weaker when compared to our other fiscal quarters of the corresponding year. &nbsp;The seasonality of our business is a result of a variety of factors, including holiday seasons, consumer demand, economic conditions and other factors beyond our control. &nbsp;As we cannot predict or influence these factors, we cannot be certain that the seasonal trends will continue in future periods as they have in our historical operating patterns.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>17</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Currency devaluations in the foreign markets in which we operate could decrease demand for our services.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We denominate some of our foreign sales in U.S. dollars. &nbsp;Consequently, decreases in the value of local currencies relative to the U.S. dollar in the markets in which we operate could adversely affect the demand for our services by increasing the price of our services in the currencies of the countries in which they are sold.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Currency fluctuations in the foreign markets in which we operate could result in currency translation exchange gains or losses or could increase or decrease the book value of our net assets.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Appreciation or depreciation in the value of local currencies relative to the U.S. dollar in the markets in which we operate will result in currency translation exchange gains or losses, which, if the appreciation or depreciation is significant, could be material. &nbsp;Additionally, the revenues, expenses, assets and liabilities of our international operations are denominated in each country&#146;s local currency. &nbsp;As such, when the value of those revenues, expenses, assets and liabilities are translated into U.S. dollars, foreign currency exchange rates may adversely affect our results of operations and the book value of our net assets.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our effective income tax rate will impact our results of operations, our cash flows and our profitability.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a global company, we generate taxable income in different countries throughout the world, with different effective income tax rates. &nbsp;Our future effective income tax rate will be impacted by a number of factors, including the geographical composition of our worldwide taxable income. &nbsp;If the United States or foreign tax authorities were to change applicable tax laws or successfully challenge the manner in which our income taxes are currently recognized, our effective income tax rate could increase, which would adversely impact our cash flow and profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>If we fail to develop, deploy and integrate financial and operational information technology systems or if we fail to upgrade or replace our information technology systems to handle increased volumes and levels of complexity, meet the demands of our customers and protect against disruptions of our operations, our business may be seriously harmed.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We are undertaking various initiatives to upgrade the information technology systems supporting our services in order to improve operational efficiencies and increase connectivity with our customers&#146; and trading partners&#146; systems in a timely and cost-effective manner. &nbsp;The failure of the hardware or software that supports our information technology systems, the loss of data contained in the systems, or the inability to access or interact with our customers electronically through our web site could significantly disrupt our operations, prevent customers from placing orders or cause us to lose customers. &nbsp;If our information technology systems are unable to manage additional volume for our operations as our business grows, our service levels and operating efficiency could decline. &nbsp;If we fail to hire and retain qualified personnel to implement, maintain and protect our information technology systems, or if we fail to upgrade our systems to meet demands of our customers, our business could be seriously harmed.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>If we fail to protect our confidential information, including our intellectual property rights, we may lose market share and our financial condition may be materially adversely affected.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We rely on a combination of copyright, trademark and trade secret laws and confidentiality procedures to protect our intellectual property rights and other confidential information. &nbsp;These protections may not be sufficient, and they do not prevent independent third parties from developing competitive products and services. &nbsp;A failure to protect our confidential information from unauthorized use or disclosure could diminish the value of our confidential information and our financial condition may be materially adversely affected.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>18</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Heightened security measures as a result of terrorist threats have created economic, political and regulatory uncertainties, some of which may materially harm our business and prospects and our ability to conduct business.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The national and global responses to terrorist threats, including heightened security measures, may materially and adversely affect us in ways we cannot currently predict. &nbsp;Some of the possible future effects include reduced business activity by our customers, changes in security measures or regulatory requirements for air travel and reductions in available commercial flights that may increase our costs or make it more difficult for us to arrange for the transport of our customers&#146; freight and increased credit and business risk for customers in industries affected by heightened security measures and threats of additional terrorist attacks.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:4226.585pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our ability to serve our customers depends on the availability of cargo space from other parties.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our ability to serve our customers depends on the availability of air and sea cargo space, including space on passenger and cargo airlines and ocean carriers that service the transportation lanes that we use. &nbsp;Shortages of cargo space are most likely to develop during holidays (with increased consumer spending) and in especially heavy transportation lanes (such as in Asia). &nbsp;In addition, available cargo space could be reduced as a result of decreases in the number of passenger airlines or ocean carriers serving particular transportation lanes at particular times. &nbsp;This could occur as a result of economic conditions, transportation strikes, regulatory changes and other factors beyond our control. &nbsp;Our future operating results could be adversely affected by significant shortages of suitable cargo space and associated changes in policies such as increases in rates and the cost of fuel, taxes and labor charged by passenger airlines or ocean carriers for cargo space.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>We are subject to market pricing by our suppliers (airlines, ocean carriers, and trucking companies). &nbsp;If we are not able to pass these costs on to our customers, our profitability will be impacted.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>&#147;Sell&#148; rates to our major customers are normally agreed upon for the term of the contract, with provisions allowing for fuel, war and security surcharges. &nbsp;The prices we pay for cargo space with our major suppliers is dependent on our volumes and relationships with our suppliers. &nbsp;If our relationships deteriorate or there are changes in management with our suppliers or with us that negatively impact such relationships, we may be unable to negotiate similar rates with our suppliers for such cargo space.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>We may lose business to competitors.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Competition within the freight industry is intense. &nbsp;We compete in North America primarily with fully integrated carriers and smaller freight-forwarders. &nbsp;Internationally, we compete primarily with the major European based freight forwarders, Expeditors International, DHL, BAX, UPS and other freight forwarders. &nbsp;We expect to encounter continued competition from those forwarders that have a predominantly international focus and have established international networks, including those based in the United States and Europe. &nbsp;We also expect to continue to encounter competition from other forwarders with nationwide networks, regional and local forwarders, passenger and cargo air carriers, trucking companies, cargo sales agents and brokers, and carriers and associations of shippers organized for the purpose of consolidating their members&#146; shipments to obtain lower freight rates from carriers. &nbsp;As a customs broker and ocean freight forwarder, we encounter strong competition in every port in which we do business, often competing with large domestic and foreign firms as well as local and regional firms. &nbsp;Our inability to compete successfully in our industry could cause us to lose customers or realize declines volume of our shipments.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our industry is consolidating and if we are unable to gain sufficient market presence in our industry, we may not be able to compete successfully against larger companies in our industry.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>19</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>There has been an increasing trend in our industry toward consolidation of the niche players and larger companies, which are attempting to increase their global operations through the acquisition of freight forwarders and contract logistics providers. &nbsp;If we are unable to gain sufficient market share in our industry through internal growth, we may not be able to compete successfully against larger companies in our industry.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our success depends on the efforts of our founder and other key managers and personnel.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our founder, James R. Crane, continues to serve as Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of Directors. &nbsp;We believe that our success is highly dependent on the continuing efforts of Mr. Crane and other executive officers and key employees, as well as our ability to attract and retain other skilled managers and personnel. &nbsp;The loss of the services of any of our key personnel could have a material adverse effect on us.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>If we are unable to limit our exposure for customers&#146; claims through contract terms and insurance coverage, we could be required to pay large amounts as compensation for their claims and our results of operations could be materially adversely affected.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Typically, we limit our liability in contracts with our customers for loss or damage to their goods. &nbsp;However, as a freight forwarder, the airline or ocean carriers that we use generally assume the same responsibility to us as we assume to our customers. &nbsp;When we act in the capacity of an authorized agent for an air or ocean carrier, the carrier, rather than us, assumes liability for the safe delivery of the customer&#146;s cargo to its ultimate destination. &nbsp;We have, from time to time, made payments to customers for claims related to our services. &nbsp;Should we experience an increase in the number of such claims or an increase in liability pursuant to claims or unfavorable resolution of claims, our results could be adversely affected. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that our insurance coverage will provide us with adequate coverage for such claims or that the maximum amount for which we are liable in connection with our services will not change in the future. &nbsp;In addition, significant increases in insurance costs as a result of claims arising from our services could reduce our profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>We are subject to claims arising from our pick up and delivery operations.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We use the services of thousands of drivers in connection with our local pick up and delivery operations. &nbsp;From time to time, these drivers are involved in accidents. &nbsp;Although most of these drivers are independent contractors, we could be held liable for their actions. &nbsp;Claims against us may exceed the amount of insurance coverage. &nbsp;A material increase in the frequency or severity of accidents, liability claims or workers&#146; compensation claims, or unfavorable resolutions of claims, could materially adversely affect us. &nbsp;In addition, significant increases in insurance costs as a result of these claims could reduce our profitability.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>We could incur additional expenses or taxes if the independent owner/operators we use in connection with our local pick up and delivery operations are found to be &#147;employees&#148; rather than &#147;independent contractors.&#148;</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Internal Revenue Service, state authorities and other third parties have at times successfully asserted that independent owner/operators in the transportation industry, including those of the type we use in connection with our local pick up and delivery operations, are &#147;employees&#148; rather than &#147;independent contractors.&#148; &nbsp;Although we believe that the independent owner/operators we use are not employees, and have tailored our program specifically to avoid this categorization, the IRS, state authorities or others could challenge this position, and federal and state tax or other applicable laws, or interpretations of applicable laws, could change. &nbsp;If they do, we could incur additional employee benefit-related expenses and could be liable for additional taxes, penalties and interest for prior periods and additional taxes for future periods.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>20</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>The failure of our policies and procedures which are designed to prevent the unlawful transportation or storage of hazardous, explosive or illegal materials could subject us to large fines, penalties or lawsuits.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We are subject to a broad range of foreign and domestic (including state and local) environmental, health and safety and criminal laws and regulations, including those governing discharges into the air and water, the storage, handling and disposal of solid and hazardous waste and the shipment of explosive or illegal substances. &nbsp;In the course of our operations, we may be asked to arrange for the storage or transportation of substances defined as hazardous under applicable laws. &nbsp;As is the case with any such operation, if a release of hazardous substances occurs on or from our facilities or from the transporter, we may be required to participate in the remedy of, or otherwise bear liability for, such release or be subject to claims from third parties whose property or person is injured by the release. &nbsp;In addition, if our employees arrange for the storage or transportation of hazardous, explosive or illegal materials in violation of applicable laws or regulations, we may face civil or criminal fines or penalties, including bans on making future shipments in particular geographic areas. &nbsp;In the event we are found to not be in compliance with applicable environmental, health and safety laws and regulations or there is a future finding that our policies and procedures fail to satisfy requisite minimum safeguards or otherwise do not comply with applicable laws or regulations, we could be subject to large fines, penalties or lawsuits.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our failure to comply with governmental permit and licensing requirements could result in substantial fines or revocation of our operating authorities, and changes in these requirements could adversely affect us.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our operations are subject to various state, local, federal and foreign regulations that in many instances require permits and licenses. &nbsp;Moreover, costs for security as a result of governmental regulations that have been and will be adopted in response to terrorist activities and potential terrorist activities, government deregulation efforts, &#147;modernization&#148; of the regulations governing customs clearance and changes in the international trade and tariff environment could require material expenditures or otherwise adversely affect us. &nbsp;We may not be able to pass these increased costs on to our customers in the form of rate increases or surcharges. &nbsp;We cannot predict what impact future regulations may have on our business. &nbsp;Our failure to maintain required permits or licenses, or to comply with applicable regulations, could result in substantial fines or revocation of our operating authorities.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Our chairman beneficially owns approximately 21.7% of our outstanding common stock and has the greatest influence of any of our stockholders.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>James R. Crane beneficially owns approximately 21.7% of our outstanding common stock. &nbsp;Based on the ownership positions of our current stockholders, his ability to influence matters submitted to a vote of stockholders is greater than any other stockholder.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Provisions of our charter, bylaws and shareholder rights plan and of Texas law may delay or prevent transactions that would benefit stockholders.</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our articles of incorporation and bylaws and Texas law contain provisions that may have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a change of control. &nbsp;These provisions, among other things:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>authorize our Board of Directors to set the terms of preferred stock;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:49.5pt; text-indent:-13.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; padding-left:49.5pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>provide that any stockholder who wishes to propose any business or to nominate a person or persons for the election as director at any meeting of stockholders may do so only if advance notice is given to our corporate secretary;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>21</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>restrict the ability of stockholders to take action by written consent; and</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:49.7pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>restrict our ability to engage in transactions with some 20% stockholders.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Because of these provisions, persons considering unsolicited tender offers or other unilateral takeover proposals may be more likely to negotiate with our board of directors rather than pursue non-negotiated takeover attempts. &nbsp;In addition, we have adopted a shareholder rights plan that will cause substantial dilution to any person or group that attempts to acquire us without the approval of our board of directors. &nbsp;The provisions of our charter, bylaws and shareholder rights plan may make it more difficult for our stockholders to benefit from transactions that are opposed by an incumbent board of directors.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc512306392"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306458"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306606"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306667"></A><A NAME="_Toc1542916"></A><A NAME="_Toc35422465"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 1B.</B></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 2.</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B><I>Properties</I></B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The properties used in our domestic and foreign operations consist principally of air and ocean freight forwarding offices, customs brokerage offices and warehouse and distribution facilities. &nbsp;Our freight forwarding terminal locations are typically located at or near major metropolitan airports and occupy between 1,000 and 509,000 square feet of leased or owned space and typically consist of offices, warehouse space, bays for loading and unloading and facilities for packing. &nbsp;Terminals are managed by a station manager who is assisted by operation managers. &nbsp;We also have locations that are limited to sales and administrative activities. &nbsp;The leased terminals are under noncancelable leases that expire on various dates through 2025. &nbsp;From time to time, we may expand or relocate terminals to accommodate growth.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>For further information regarding our lease commitments, see note 16 of the notes to our consolidated financial statements.</P>
<A NAME="_Toc507922805"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937513"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937709"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937892"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306393"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306459"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306607"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306668"></A><A NAME="_Toc1542917"></A><A NAME="_Toc35422466"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 3.</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B><I>Legal Proceedings</I></B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In December 1997, the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (&#147;EEOC&#148;) issued a Commissioner&#146;s Charge alleging violations under Title VII, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, and the Equal Pay Act.&nbsp; In May through July 2000, eight individuals filed suit against us in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, alleging gender, race and national origin discrimination, as well as sexual harassment.&nbsp; The individual plaintiffs sought to certify a class of approximately 1,000 of our current and former employees and applicants. &nbsp;The case was&nbsp;eventually transferred to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas &#150; Houston Division. </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>22</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On October 2, 2001, we and the EEOC announced the filing of a Consent Decree settlement, under which we agreed to pay $8.5 million into a fund to compensate individuals who claim to have experienced discrimination (&#147;Settlement Fund&#148;). &nbsp;In addition, we agreed to contribute $500,000 to establish a Leadership Development Program (&#147;LDP&#148;). &nbsp;The Consent Decree expired on October 3, 2005, with &nbsp;the Claims administration process under the Consent Decree completed by EGL and the EEOC in early 2005. &nbsp;Of the 2,073 claims received, only 203 were deemed to be eligible for a monetary distribution totaling $903,000. &nbsp;On February 10, 2005, upon motion by EGL and the EEOC, the Court entered an Order directing that EGL recapture $6.0 million plus accrued interest from the Settlement Fund, which release of such&nbsp;funds resulted in $6.0 million in income in the first quarter of 2005. &nbsp;The Court also approved the parties&#146; agreement to transfer $1.4 million to the LDP.&nbsp; From that amount, EGL has reimbursed itself $582,000 for corporate funds previously expended on LDP expenses. &nbsp;The Court further approved the parties&#146; agreement to retain $1.1 million in the Settlement Fund for the payment of eligible claims.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Through March 13, 2006, 176 eligible Claimants have been sent settlement checks totaling $825,000. &nbsp;Only two Claimants have opted out of the settlement. &nbsp;Eligible claimants also had the option of objecting to an award, but to do so they must have notified the Claims Administrator within thirty days of the date of their eligibility notice. &nbsp;To date, all objections have been resolved by agreement between the EEOC and counsel for EGL. &nbsp;If any funds remain in the Settlement Fund after payment of all claims, the remainder shall be deposited in the LDP.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>To the extent any of the individual plaintiffs or any other persons who have opted out of the settlement pursue individual claims, we intend to continue to vigorously defend against their allegations. &nbsp;We currently expect to prevail in our defense of any remaining individual claims. &nbsp;There can be no assurance as to what amount of time it will take to resolve any other lawsuits and related issues or the degree of any adverse affect these matters may have on our financial condition and results of operations. &nbsp;A substantial settlement payment or judgment could result in a significant decrease in our working capital and liquidity and recognition of a loss in our consolidated statement of income.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>During 2003 and 2004, EGL acted as a logistics subcontractor in the Middle East to Kellogg Brown &amp; Root, Inc. (&#147;KBR&#148;), which as general contractor provided various services to the U.S. Department of Defense (&#147;DOD&#148;) and other U.S. government agencies. &nbsp;In 2004, we received an administrative subpoena from the Office of Inspector General of the DOD requesting documents relating to the billing of war risk surcharges by EGL on certain shipments of KBR freight in the period from late 2003 to mid-2004. &nbsp;EGL cooperated fully with the government&#146;s request and its investigation. &nbsp;In the course of our internal investigation of the matter, we reviewed documents related to the imposition of war risk surcharges on EGL by transportation providers. &nbsp;EGL uncovered evidence suggesting that certain documents related to the imposition of war risk surcharges on EGL, that were then charged to KBR, were false and the charges were not warranted. &nbsp;Following this discovery, and with approval from the government, we engaged auditors to conduct a forensic analysis of war risk surcharges charged by EGL. &nbsp;This analysis concluded that approximately $1.1 million of war risk surcharges charged by EGL were not actually imposed on EGL by transportation providers. &nbsp;We provided the results of this investigation to the government and promptly terminated two employees for violation of EGL&#146;s Code of Conduct.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a result of discussions with the government, we received a letter from the United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas on December 12, 2005 offering to settle the war risk surcharge issue for the sum of $4.0 million. &nbsp;Of the $4.0 million, $1.1 million reimburses the government for war risk surcharges (the full amount of which had been previously reserved in EGL&#146;s financial statements), and the remaining $2.9 million represents penalties for improper billings. &nbsp;EGL has agreed to reimburse the $1.1 million in war risk surcharges, and expects to reach agreement with the government promptly on the timing and final amount of the penalties. &nbsp;Recognizing EGL&#146;s cooperation in and assistance with the government&#146;s review, as part of the settlement, the United States Attorneys Office and the Defense Criminal Investigative Service is expected to agree to waive all investigatory expenses and make no recommendation to the DOD for debarment of EGL from future DOD contracts. &nbsp;In addition, the </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>23</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<P style="page-break-before:never; margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas is not expected to recommend to the DOD or the Department of Justice any criminal indictment of EGL related to the war risk surcharges. &nbsp;In December 2005, EGL recorded a charge of $2.9 million (approximately $0.06 per share) for this penalty.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In February 2006, we were notified by the U.S. Army&#146;s Office of Suspension and Debarment that we were temporarily suspended from doing business with the government as a direct contractor or sub-contractor effective February 27, 2006. &nbsp;The basis of the suspension was the guilty plea entered by one of the two employees EGL terminated related to the war risk surcharge investigation. &nbsp;This suspension does not include business previously awarded with a signed contract, business using tenders, tariffs or quotes, or sub-contractors less than $25,000. &nbsp;This action was taken despite the settlement offer by the United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas in which it offered not to recommend that EGL be debarred from future DOD contracts. &nbsp;The suspension is pending an appeal to the U.S. Army&#146;s Suspension and Debarment Officer.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>At the request of the government, EGL limited its internal investigation and its public statements on these matters so as not to interfere with the government&#146;s broader investigation.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>One former and two current independent contractor pickup and delivery (&#147;P&amp;D&#148;) drivers filed a complaint in California state court on September 12, 2005, on behalf of themselves and similarly situated drivers in California alleging various causes of action based on their theory that the drivers are employees and not independent contractors. &nbsp;The complaint requests (i) the matter be designated as a class action on behalf of all independent contractor P&amp;D drivers working for EGL in California; (ii) a declaratory judgment that EGL has violated the law; (iii) an equitable accounting and an unspecified amount of damages; and (iv) restitution in the form of business expenses, unpaid overtime, meal period compensation, unlawful deductions from wages, statutory penalties, interest, attorneys&#146; fees and costs. We removed the case to federal district court for the Northern District of California, and the parties have agreed to focus only on the individual claims of the three named defendants in the first phase of the proceedings. &nbsp;In the event one or more of the plaintiffs&#146; claims survive the summary judgment phase, the next phase would focus on whether the action is maintainable as a class action. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend this lawsuit and believe that plaintiffs are properly classified as independent contractors.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In addition, we are party to routine litigation incidental to our business, which primarily involves employment matters or claims for goods lost or damaged in transit or improperly shipped. &nbsp;Many of the other lawsuits to which we are a party are covered by insurance and are being defended by our insurance carriers. &nbsp;We have established accruals for these other matters and it is management&#146;s opinion that resolution of such litigation will not have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position. &nbsp;However, a substantial settlement payment or judgment in excess of our accruals could have a material adverse effect on our consolidated results of operations or cash flows.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>No matters were submitted to a vote of security holders during the fourth quarter of our fiscal year ended December 31, 2005.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><B>Dividends</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Since our initial public offering in November 1995, EGL has not paid cash dividends on our common stock. &nbsp;It is the current intention of our management to retain earnings to finance the growth of our business in lieu of paying dividends. &nbsp;Our credit facility and senior, secured notes contain covenants that restrict our ability to pay dividends unless we maintain certain leverage ratios. &nbsp;See Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#151; Liquidity and Capital Resources for a discussion of our credit facility.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>ITEM 7.</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B><I>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</I></B></P>
<A NAME="_Toc507937522"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937718"></A><A NAME="_Toc507937901"></A><A NAME="_Toc512306402"></A><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The following management&#146;s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this report. &nbsp;In addition, for information on our critical accounting policies and the judgment made in their application, please read &#147;Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates&#148; beginning on page 43.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Overview</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The primary macroeconomic growth indicators of our business include general growth in the economy, international trade, particularly out of Asia, the level of high-tech spending and the increase in outsourcing of logistics projects. &nbsp;Business drivers that we control and focus on internally are our ability to: &nbsp;(i) link transportation services with our logistics services, (ii) cross-sell our services to existing and prospective customers and (iii) collaborate with our customers to provide flexible, cost-effective and profitable supply chain solutions.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>We achieved revenues of $3.10 billion for the year ended December 31, 2005, a 13% increase over revenues of $2.74 billion in 2004. &nbsp;Our financial position was strengthened by record gross and net revenues throughout 2005. &nbsp;Despite growth in our business, we remain committed to leveraging our infrastructure by seeking to contain our operating expenses and improving our yield management in 2006. </P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Our results of operations in 2005 were impacted by, among other things, the following:</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>leveraging our global network to increase volumes across all service offerings and geographic divisions;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>improved volumes in the North America forwarding market;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>high effective tax rate due to fully reserved deferred tax benefits for foreign net operating losses;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>foreign exchange gains of $2.5 million; </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>recapture of $6.0 million plus accrued interest of the EEOC Settlement Fund;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>$2.9 million penalty for improper government billings;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>a pre-tax charge of $1.6 million for workforce reductions, mainly in certain European and USA locations; </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10.5pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>$4.0 million gain from the receipt of escrow proceeds from the 2004 sale of our investment in TDS Logistics, Inc.;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>the repurchase of 5.0 million shares for $94.3 million under our share repurchase program;</P>

<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>warehouse fire in our U.K. operations; </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>$4.0 million in insurance claims activity;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>improved working capital management to increase cash flows from operating activities; and</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>continuing the deployment of information technology systems globally.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Leveraging our global network</I>. &nbsp;In 2005, we leveraged our global network and our ability to cross-sell services to increase volumes for all of our service offerings in all geographic divisions. &nbsp;In addition, our balanced product offering enabled us to provide flexible solutions to our customers both domestically and internationally. &nbsp;In 2005, we continued to leverage our low cost North America network and customer base, as customers increasingly moved products from overseas&#146; manufacturing facilities directly to U.S. distribution and retail centers.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>North America forwarding market</I>. &nbsp;Deferred shipment (third through fifth day) volumes increased by 19.0% in 2005 versus an increase of 3.0% in 2004 and priority (next flight out, next day or second day) volumes decreased 8.6% in 2005 versus an increase of 1.9% in 2004. &nbsp;In addition, U.S. imports and exports continue to increase, reflecting the strength of the U.S. economy and the continued shift of production overseas. The improvement in domestic shipment volumes added significantly to our increase in gross revenues during the year and improved results of operations. &nbsp;Our 2005 results continue to highlight the ability of our low cost domestic model to generate domestic growth with a mix of priority and deferred shipments.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Income tax</I>. &nbsp;The effective tax rate for 2005 was 42.2%, due to fully reserved deferred tax benefits for foreign net operating losses. &nbsp;Our effective tax rates fluctuate due to changes in the level of pre-tax income in foreign countries that have different rates and certain income and/or expenses that are permanently non-taxable or non-deductible in certain jurisdictions.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Foreign exchange impact on results of operations</I>. &nbsp;Our cash flows and net income are subject to fluctuations due to changes in exchange rates. We provide services to customers in locations throughout the world and, as a result, operate with many currencies, including the key currencies of North America, South America, Asia, the South Pacific and Europe. &nbsp;In 2005, we recognized $2.5 million of net foreign exchange gains primarily due to gains in Brazil and European countries.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Recapture of EEOC Settlement Fund</I>. &nbsp;In February 2005, in response to a joint motion filed by EGL and the EEOC, a U.S. District Court ordered the return of $6.0 million to us of $8.5 million previously held in a fund to resolve potential claims in connection with a 2001 consent decree (see note 15 of the notes to our consolidated financial statements). &nbsp;The joint motion and subsequent order resulted in $6.0 million in income in the first quarter of 2005.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Government billings</I>. &nbsp;In the fourth quarter of 2005, we recorded a $2.9 million penalty for improper war risk surcharge billings to Kellogg Brown &amp; Root, Inc. (KBR).</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:4226.585pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Workforce reductions. &nbsp;</I>In the second quarter of 2005, we eliminated approximately 350 full-time, part-time and contractor positions primarily in the United States and Europe as part of a cost reduction plan. &nbsp;The workforce reduction resulted in a pre-tax charge of approximately $1.6 million during the second quarter of 2005 for termination benefits. &nbsp;All amounts were paid by the end of the third quarter of 2005 and there are no remaining liabilities under this plan.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Gain from sale of TDS Logistics, Inc</I>. &nbsp;In 2005, we recorded a gain of $4.0 million related to our 2004 sale of TDS Logistics, Inc. following the resolution of certain contingencies held in escrow.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=center>28</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
