<P style="page-break-before:never; margin:0pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=center><B>EGL, INC.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=center><B>Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=center><B>December 31, 2005 and 2004</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:8pt" align=center><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a result of stock option exercises for the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003 of non-qualified stock options to purchase an aggregate of 1.0 million, 2.1 million and 324,000 shares of common stock, respectively, the Company is entitled to a federal and state income tax deduction of approximately $12.1 million, $19.2 million and $1.4 million, respectively, with a related reduction in its federal and state tax obligations of approximately $5.0 million, $7.8 million and $474,000, respectively. &nbsp;Accordingly, the Company recorded an increase to additional paid-in capital and a reduction in current taxes payable. &nbsp;Any exercises of non-qualified stock options in the future at exercise prices below the then fair market value of the common stock may also result in tax deductions equal to the difference between such amounts, although there can be no assurance as to whether or not such exercises will occur, the amount of any deductions or the Company&#146;s ability to fully utilize such tax deductions.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Company&#146;s U.S. federal income tax returns from fiscal years 2000 to 2001 are currently subject to examination by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). &nbsp;On April 8, 2005, the Company received a Revenue Agent Report from the IRS field examination team for which the Company was required to respond by May 16, 2005. &nbsp;On May 16th, the Company responded with a protest in response to the Agents Report contesting the proposed adjustments. &nbsp;On June 8th, the IRS prepared a rebuttal report to the Company&#146;s protest for which no issues were resolved and the IRS examination team subsequently forwarded the case to the Appeals division of the IRS for resolution. &nbsp;The Company attended an exparte conference with the IRS examination and appeals teams on November 15, 2005, officially beginning the appeals process. &nbsp;The Company submitted additional technical arguments for its return positions to the appeals team on January 10, 2006. &nbsp;No meetings with Appeals have occurred to date. &nbsp;The income tax returns that are under audit are the income tax returns filed by EGL for fiscal years ended September 30, 2000, September 30, 2001, December 31, 2001, and the final income tax return filed by Circle International Group, Inc., a subsidiary of EGL, Inc., for the fiscal year ended October 2, 2000, when it was a separate company prior to the merger with EGL, Inc. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Specifically, the IRS is proposing to disallow various merger transaction costs taken as tax deductions related to the merger of EGL and Circle, and to allocate certain merger and selling, general and administrative expenses to all of its foreign affiliates which were taken as tax deductions on the 2000 and 2001 fiscal return years for both EGL and Circle. &nbsp;The IRS is also proposing to disallow the deduction of various software research and development expenditures that were taken as tax deductions on the 2000 and 2001 fiscal tax returns for EGL.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>If the proposed adjustments were upheld, the Company would be required to pay a total amount of approximately $14 million in cash taxes, of which approximately $6.5 million would impact the consolidated statement of income, plus accrued interest of approximately $4.9 million through December 31, 2005. &nbsp;No penalties have been proposed by the IRS as part of this examination. &nbsp;Interest will continue to accrue until the matters are resolved. &nbsp;The Company believes that the matters raised by the IRS were properly reported on its U.S. federal income tax returns in accordance with applicable laws and regulations in effect during the tax periods involved and is challenging these adjustments vigorously. &nbsp;While the outcome of proceedings for these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, the Company believes that its U.S. federal income tax returns were completed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and does not believe material adjustments to its tax returns are probable at this time. &nbsp;However there is no assurance that the final outcome of the future proceedings with the IRS will not result in material adjustments which would have a material adverse impact on the Company&#146;s results of operations, financial position and cash flows.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Company is also subject to tax audits in certain of its foreign and domestic jurisdictions and management believes such returns have been filed in accordance with tax laws in effect at the time. &nbsp;However, there is no assurance that such audits will not result in future adjustments.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 11 &#150; Stockholders&#146; equity </B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Share repurchase program</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On February 25, 2004, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase and retirement of up to $15 million of its outstanding common stock over the 120 days following adoption of the repurchase program (the Program). &nbsp;On March 5, 2004, the Board of Directors approved an increase in the maximum value of shares to be repurchased from $15 million to up to $65 million and extended the Program to July 3, 2004. &nbsp;The Company repurchased and retired 3.4 million shares at an average price of $17.37 per share for approximately $59.1 million under this authorization.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On April 4, 2005, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors adopted a stock repurchase program to repurchase up to $60 million of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock depending on market conditions and other factors with an expiration date of August 4, 2005. &nbsp;On May 31, 2005, the Board of Directors approved an increase in the maximum dollar amount of shares to be repurchased from $60 million to $120 million and extended the expiration date to September 28, 2005. &nbsp;As of September 28, 2005, the Company has repurchased a total of 5.0 million shares at an average price of $18.98 per share for approximately $94.3 million.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On August 29, 2005, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized a modified &#147;Dutch Auction&#148; self-tender offer to purchase up to 9,615,000 shares (up to $250 million) of its common stock, representing approximately 20% of its approximately 47.2 million outstanding shares as of August 24, 2005. &nbsp;The tender offer commenced on Tuesday, August 30, 2005 and expired on Wednesday, September 28, 2005. &nbsp;In the tender offer, shareholders had the opportunity to tender some or all of their shares at a price not less than $22.50 per share or more than $26.00 per share, net to the seller in cash, without interest.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On October 4, 2005, the Company announced the final results of the tender offer. &nbsp;An aggregate of 8,085,958 shares were properly tendered and not withdrawn at or below a price of $26.00. &nbsp;Because shareholders tendered less than 9,615,000 shares, there was no proration of tendered shares. &nbsp;The Company financed the tender offer with the use of cash on hand and borrowings of $196.0 million under both the new $300.0 million line of credit facility and the $100.0 million bridge loan that was refinanced by the issuance of $100.0 million of floating rate senior secured notes due in October 2012 (See Note 8). &nbsp;As a result, EGL accepted for purchase and paid approximately $211.0 million for all 8,085,958 shares at a price of $26.00 per share. &nbsp;Any shares received in the tender offer that were not tendered properly were returned to the tendering shareholders. &nbsp;The shares purchased pursuant to the tender offer represented approximately 17.1% of EGL&#146;s outstanding shares as of September 30, 2005.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Treasury stock</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>During 2005, 2004 and 2003, 90,000, 57,000 and 54,000 shares, respectively, were reissued to satisfy obligations to issue common shares relating to the Company&#146;s Employee Stock Purchase Plan (Note 12) and restricted stock awards. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005 and 2004, 5.8 million and 926,000 shares, respectively, were held in treasury. &nbsp;The Company accounts for treasury stock using the cost method.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In June 2005, May 2004 and November 2003, the Company issued 14,000 shares, 14,000 shares and 11,000 shares, respectively, of restricted common stock to certain members of its Board of Directors. &nbsp;The Company recorded these shares as unearned compensation of $270,000, $315,000 and $185,000, respectively, at the date of the awards based on the quoted fair market value of the shares at the time the awards were granted. &nbsp;These amounts are amortized over the twelve-month vesting period of the awards.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In December 2004, the Company agreed to issue up to 75,000 shares of restricted common stock to its executive officers and other key employees contingent upon the Company achieving certain annual earnings per share (EPS) targets for 2005. &nbsp;The minimum EPS target was not met for 2005; therefore, no shares were issued under this award. &nbsp;In March 2006, the Company expects to issue 38,000 shares of restricted common stock to certain executive officers and other key employees. &nbsp;One-fifth of the restricted shares will vest in March 2006. &nbsp;The remaining restricted shares will then vest in four equal installments in December of the years 2006 through 2009. &nbsp;Upon vesting, the shares of common stock of the Company awarded as set forth above shall have no further restrictions. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also issued 10,000 shares of restricted common stock to an employee as of October 31, 2005. &nbsp;Unearned compensation expense of $280,000 was recorded at the date of the award based on the quoted fair market value of the shares and is being amortized over the three-year vesting period of the award.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Preferred stock rights</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On May 23, 2001, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors declared a dividend of one right to purchase preferred stock (Right) for each outstanding share of the Company&#146;s common stock to shareholders of record at the close of business on June 4, 2001. &nbsp;Each Right initially entitles the registered holder to purchase from the Company a fractional share consisting of one one-thousandth of a share of Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a purchase price of $120 per fractional share, subject to adjustment. &nbsp;The Rights generally will not become exercisable until ten days after a public announcement that a person or group has acquired 15% or more of the Company&#146;s common stock (thereby becoming an &#147;Acquiring Person&#148;) or the commencement of a tender or exchange offer that would result in an Acquiring Person (the earlier of such dates being called the &#147;Distribution Date&#148;). &nbsp;James R. Crane, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of EGL, will not become an Acquiring Person unless and until he and his affiliates become the beneficial owner of 49% or more of the common stock. &nbsp;Rights will be issued with all shares of the Company&#146;s common stock issued from the record date to the Distribution Date. &nbsp;Until the Distribution Date, the Rights will be evidenced by the certificates representing the Company&#146;s common stock and will be transferable only with the common stock. &nbsp;Generally, if any person or group becomes an Acquiring Person, each Right, other than Rights beneficially owned by the Acquiring Person (which will thereupon become void), will thereafter entitle its holder to purchase, at the Rights&#146; then current exercise price, shares of the Company&#146;s common stock having a market value of two times the exercise price of the Right. &nbsp;If, after there is an Acquiring Person, and the Company or a majority of its assets is acquired in certain transactions, each Right not owned by an Acquiring Person will entitle its holder to purchase, at a discount, shares of common stock of the acquiring entity (or its parent) in the transaction. &nbsp;At any time until ten days after a public announcement that the rights have been triggered, the Company will generally be entitled to redeem the Rights for $0.01 and to amend the rights in any manner other than to change the redemption price. &nbsp;Certain subsequent amendments are also permitted. &nbsp;The Rights expire on June 4, 2011.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 12 &#150; Employee benefit and stock option plans</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Defined contribution plan</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Company maintains the EGL, Inc. 401(k) Plan (the EGL Plan) pursuant to which the Company provides up to dollar for dollar discretionary matching of employee tax-deferred savings up to a maximum of 5% of eligible compensation for employees in the United States. &nbsp;Each participant vests in the Company&#146;s contribution over the course of five years at a vesting rate of 20% per year. &nbsp;During the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, the Company recorded charges of $2.0 million and $800,000, respectively, each year related to discretionary contributions to this plan. &nbsp;No charges were recorded for the EGL Plan during the year ended December 31, 2003 due to use of forfeitures.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Additionally, certain of the Company&#146;s international subsidiaries have governmental or discretionary defined contribution plans with contribution rates ranging from 2.00% to 17.32% of eligible compensation. &nbsp;For the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, the Company recorded charges of $2.2 million, $1.8 million and $1.6 million, respectively, related to discretionary and mandatory contributions to these plans.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Defined benefit plans</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Certain of the Company&#146;s international subsidiaries sponsor defined benefit pension plans covering certain full-time employees. &nbsp;Benefits are based on the employee&#146;s years of service and compensation. &nbsp;The Company&#146;s plans are funded in conformity with the funding requirements of applicable government regulations of the country in which the plans are located. &nbsp;These foreign plans are not subject to the United States Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. &nbsp;Information for the Company&#146;s defined benefit plans is provided below.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Stock purchase plan</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In 1999, the Company initiated an employee stock purchase plan in order to provide eligible employees of the Company and its participating subsidiaries, including subsidiaries based outside of the United States, with the opportunity to purchase the Company&#146;s common stock through payroll deductions. &nbsp;Employees may purchase common stock under this plan during a six-month offering period based on a formula provided in the plan document, which generally allows the Company&#146;s employees to purchase common stock at 85% of quoted fair market value. &nbsp;Under this plan, 550,000 shares are authorized for purchase. &nbsp;During 2005, 2004 and 2003, 66,000, 42,000 and 43,000 shares of common stock were purchased under this plan at an average price of $17.25, $18.66 and $12.52 per share, respectively.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Stock option plans</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Company has four option plans whereby certain officers, directors, and employees may be granted options, appreciation rights or awards related to the Company&#146;s common stock. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, 1.9 million shares are authorized for issuance under the Company&#146;s stock option plans.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>Circle Stock Option Plans</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The 1994 Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan and the 1999 Stock Option Plan were plans created by Circle prior to the merger with EGL. &nbsp;Options outstanding pursuant to these plans are exercisable in shares of EGL common stock and were automatically accelerated upon consummation of the merger with EGL. &nbsp;No new options were granted under these plans.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><I>EGL Plan</I></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Long-Term Incentive Plan permits the grant of stock options at an exercise price equal to the fair market value of the common stock on the date of grant. &nbsp;The plan is authorized for a maximum of 12.2 million shares. &nbsp;Options granted under the plan generally vest ratably over a three-year, five-year or seven-year period from date of grant (or 100% upon death). &nbsp;Vested options granted to date generally terminate seven years from date of grant.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Additional awards may be granted under the Long-Term Incentive Plan in the form of cash, stock, or stock appreciation rights. &nbsp;The stock appreciation right awards may consist of the right to receive payment in cash or common stock. &nbsp;Any such award may be subject to certain conditions, including continuous service with the Company or achievement of certain business objectives. &nbsp;There have been no awards of this kind issued under the Long-Term Incentive Plan.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In December 2005, the Company granted options to purchase 1.4 million shares to certain of its employees and executive officers with the number of options to be exercisable contingent upon satisfying performance vesting and time vesting criteria. &nbsp;The performance vesting of the option shares is determined based upon the Company&#146;s earnings per share (EPS) for the year ending December 31, 2006. &nbsp;Any portion of the option shares that do not satisfy the performance vesting criteria will terminate upon determining the EPS for 2006. &nbsp;The portion of the options that satisfy the performance criteria will vest over a three year period with one third vesting in March 2007 upon determination of the EPS for 2006 with the remaining shares vesting in two equal installments in December 2007 and 2008. &nbsp;The Company believes it is probable that 1.0 million of the shares will vest based upon meeting the performance criteria. &nbsp;There was no compensation expense in 2005 for these stock-based awards.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>The Director Plan provides for automatic restricted stock awards to non-employee directors at the time they join the Board and annually thereafter. &nbsp;These awards vest within one year from the date of grant and terminate ten years from date of grant. &nbsp;The plan was authorized for a maximum of 400,000 shares.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 13 &#150; Earnings per share</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Basic earnings per common share excludes dilution and is computed by dividing income available to common shareholders by the weighted average number of shares outstanding for the period. &nbsp;Diluted earnings per common share includes potential dilution that could occur if stock options were exercised or convertible debt was exchanged for common stock. &nbsp;The convertible notes were converted into 5,736,074 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock as of December 17, 2004. &nbsp;These shares have been included in basic earnings per share upon conversion and when dilutive, in diluted earnings per share prior to conversion.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 15 &#150; EEOC legal settlement</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In December 1997, the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (&#147;EEOC&#148;) issued a Commissioner&#146;s Charge alleging violations under Title VII, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, and the Equal Pay Act. &nbsp;In May through July 2000, eight individuals filed suit against the Company in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, alleging gender, race and national origin discrimination, as well as sexual harassment.&nbsp; The individual plaintiffs sought to certify a class of approximately 1,000 of the Company&#146;s current and former employees and applicants. &nbsp;The case was eventually transferred to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas &#150; Houston Division. </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On October 2, 2001, the Company and the EEOC announced the filing of a Consent Decree settlement, under which the Company agreed to pay $8.5 million into a fund to compensate individuals who claim to have experienced discrimination (&#147;Settlement Fund&#148;). &nbsp;In addition, the Company agreed to contribute $500,000 to establish a Leadership Development Program (&#147;LDP&#148;). &nbsp;The Consent Decree expired on October 3, 2005, with the Claims administration process under the Consent Decree completed by the Company and the EEOC in early 2005. &nbsp;Of the 2,073 claims received, only 203 were deemed to be eligible for a monetary distribution&nbsp;totaling&nbsp;$903,000. &nbsp;On February 10, 2005, upon motion by the Company and the EEOC, the Court entered an Order directing that the Company recapture $6.0 million plus Company accrued interest from the Settlement Fund. &nbsp;Reversal of the related accrued liability resulted in $6.0 million in income in the first quarter of 2005. &nbsp;The Court also approved the parties&#146; agreement to transfer $1.4 million to the LDP.&nbsp; From that amount, the Company has reimbursed itself $582,000 for corporate funds previously expended on LDP expenses. &nbsp;The Court further approved the parties&#146; agreement to retain $1.1 million in the Settlement Fund for the payment of eligible claims.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Through March 13, 2006, 176 eligible Claimants have been sent settlement checks totaling $825,000. &nbsp;Only two Claimants have opted out of the settlement. &nbsp;Eligible claimants also had the option of objecting to an award, but to do so they must have notified the Claims Administrator within thirty days of the date of their eligibility notice. &nbsp;To date, all objections have been resolved by agreement between the EEOC and counsel for the Company. &nbsp;If any funds remain in the Settlement Fund after payment of all claims, the remainder shall be deposited in the LDP.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR>
<BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:11pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt" align=center>F-40</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="page-break-before:never; margin:0pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=center><B>EGL, INC.</B></P>

<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>To the extent any of the individual plaintiffs or any other persons who have opted out of the settlement pursue individual claims, the Company intends to continue to vigorously defend against their allegations. &nbsp;The Company currently expects to prevail in the Company&#146;s defense of any remaining individual claims. &nbsp;There can be no assurance as to what amount of time it will take to resolve any other lawsuits and related issues or the degree of any adverse affect these matters may have on the Company&#146;s financial condition and results of operations. &nbsp;A substantial settlement payment or judgment could result in a significant decrease in the Company&#146;s working capital and liquidity and recognition of a loss in the Company&#146;s consolidated statement of income.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><B>U.K. fire damage</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On January 9, 2005, the Company&#146;s London (Thurrock) warehouse and all contents were destroyed by fire. &nbsp;At the time of the fire, the Company maintained insurance coverage for damaged property, business interruption and cargo losses with insurance limits of $35 million for damaged property and business interruption and $10 million for cargo losses. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>During the first quarter of 2005, the Company recorded a loss and recognized an insurance recovery of $721,000 for property destroyed in the fire. &nbsp;In February 2005, the Company received an interim payment on its property claim of $673,000. &nbsp;The Company incurred $1.2 million of pre-tax operating losses in the first quarter of 2005 as a result of the fire. &nbsp;A preliminary business interruption claim related to the fire has been submitted to our insurance carriers with a $928,000 initial payment received in May 2005, of which $567,000, $163,000 and $198,000 are recorded in revenues, personnel costs and other selling, general and administrative expenses, respectively, in the accompanying consolidated statement of income. &nbsp;In addition, during the fourth quarter, we incurred a $1.6 million lease surrender charge. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2005, $4.4 million of cargo claims have been settled under the Company&#146;s insurance policy. &nbsp;An additional estimated $6.4 million of claims remain open of which $5.6 million is deemed probable of recovery under the Company&#146;s insurance policy. &nbsp;The Company recorded a liability of $823,000 for the estimated claims in excess of its insurance policy limits. &nbsp;At December 31, 2005, a $5.6 million insurance receivable and a $6.4 million insurance liability for these estimated cargo losses was included in the Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet. &nbsp;However, existing claims could be settled in excess of the Company&#146;s insurance limits, which could have a material impact on its financial position, cash flows and results of operations.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><B>U.S. Government billing</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>During 2003 and 2004, the Company acted as a logistics subcontractor in the Middle East to Kellogg Brown &amp; Root, Inc. (&#147;KBR&#148;), which as general contractor provided various services to the U.S. Department of Defense (&#147;DOD&#148;) and other U.S. government agencies. &nbsp;In 2004, the Company received an administrative subpoena from the Office of Inspector General of the DOD requesting documents relating to the billing of war risk surcharges by the Company on certain shipments of KBR freight in the period from late 2003 to mid-2004. &nbsp;The Company has cooperated fully with the government&#146;s request and its investigation. &nbsp;In the course of its internal investigation of the matter, the Company reviewed documents related to the imposition of war risk surcharges on it by transportation providers. &nbsp;The Company uncovered evidence suggesting that certain documents related to the imposition of war risk surcharges on the Company, that were then charged to KBR, were false and the charges were not warranted. &nbsp;Following this discovery, and with approval from the government, the Company engaged auditors to conduct a forensic analysis of war risk surcharges charged by the Company. &nbsp;This analysis concluded that approximately $1.1 million of war risk surcharges charged by the Company were not actually imposed on the Company by transportation providers. &nbsp;The Company provided the results of this investigation to the government and promptly terminated two employees for violation of the Company&#146;s Code of Conduct.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>As a result of discussions with the government, the Company received a letter from the United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas on December 12, 2005 offering to settle the war risk surcharge issue for the sum of $4.0 million. &nbsp;Of the $4.0 million, $1.1 million reimburses the government for war risk surcharges (the full amount of which had been previously reserved in the Company&#146;s financial statements), and the remaining $2.9 million represents penalties for improper billings. &nbsp;The Company has agreed to reimburse the $1.1 million in war risk surcharges, and expects to reach agreement with the government promptly on the timing and final amount of the penalties. &nbsp;Recognizing the Company&#146;s cooperation in and assistance with the government&#146;s review, as part of the settlement, the United States Attorneys Office and the Defense Criminal Investigative Service is expected to agree to waive all investigatory expenses and make no recommendation to the DOD for debarment of the Company from future DOD contracts. &nbsp;In addition, the United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas is not expected to recommend to the DOD or the Department of Justice any criminal indictment of the Company related to the war risk surcharges. &nbsp;In December 2005, the Company recorded a charge of $2.9 million (approximately $0.06 per share) for this penalty.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In February 2006, the Company was notified by the U.S. Army&#146;s Office of Suspension and Debarment that the Company was temporarily suspended from doing business with the government as a direct contractor or sub-contractor effective February 27, 2006. &nbsp;The basis of the suspension was the guilty plea entered by one of the two employees the Company terminated related to the war risk surcharge investigation. &nbsp;This suspension does not include business previously awarded with a signed contract, business using tenders, tariffs or quotes, or sub-contractors less than $25,000. &nbsp;This action was taken despite the settlement offer by the United States Attorneys Office of the Eastern District of Texas in which it offered not to recommend that the Company be debarred from future DOD contracts. &nbsp;The suspension is pending an appeal to the U.S. Army&#146;s Suspension and Debarment Officer.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>At the request of the government, the Company limited its internal investigation and its public statements on these matters so as not to interfere with the government&#146;s broader investigation.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Litigation</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In July 2002, Kitty Hawk, Inc., a provider of air transportation services, filed a demand for binding arbitration against the Company with the American Arbitration Association to resolve its claim for freight transportation services rendered to the Company. &nbsp;In response, the Company asserted certain counterclaims. &nbsp;In July 2002, the Company recorded a liability of $1.5 million for its obligation for freight services provided by Kitty Hawk. &nbsp;Arbitration hearings were held during June 2003 and the parties submitted their final post-hearing briefs. &nbsp;In August 2003, the arbitrators ruled in favor of Kitty Hawk, awarding Kitty Hawk $3.8 million. &nbsp;In September 2003, the Company filed a motion to modify and correct the award, which was denied by the arbitrators and, therefore, the Company increased its liability to $3.8 million. &nbsp;The Company paid Kitty Hawk $2.0 million in 2003 and $1.8 million in 2004.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>One former and two current independent contractor pickup and delivery (&#147;P&amp;D&#148;) drivers filed a complaint in California state court on September 12, 2005, on behalf of themselves and similarly situated drivers in California alleging various causes of action based on their theory that the drivers are employees and not independent contractors. &nbsp;The complaint requests (i) that the matter be designated as a class action on behalf of all independent contractor P&amp;D drivers working for the Company in California; (ii) a declaratory judgment that the Company has violated the law; (iii) an equitable accounting; and (iv) an unspecified amount of damages and restitution in the form of business expenses, unpaid overtime, meal period compensation, unlawful deductions from wages, statutory penalties, interest, attorneys&#146; fees and costs. The Company removed the case to federal district court for the Northern District of California, and the parties have agreed to focus only on the individual claims of the three named defendants in the first phase of the proceedings. &nbsp;In the event one or more of the plaintiffs&#146; claims survive the summary judgment phase, the next phase would focus on whether the action is maintainable as a class action. &nbsp;The Company intends to vigorously defend this lawsuit and believes that plaintiffs are properly classified as independent contractors.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In addition, the Company is party to routine litigation incidental to its business, which primarily involves employment matters or claims for goods lost or damaged in transit or improperly shipped. &nbsp;Many of the other lawsuits to which the Company is a party are covered by insurance and are being defended by Company&#146;s insurance carriers. &nbsp;The Company has established accruals for these other matters and it is management&#146;s opinion that the resolution of such litigation will not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows. &nbsp;However, a substantial settlement payment or judgment in excess of the Company&#146;s accruals could have a material adverse effect on its consolidated results of operations or cash flows.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 17 &#150; Restructuring</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:12.5pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>In June 2005, the Company announced that it was eliminating approximately 350 full-time, part-time and contractor positions in connection with a cost reduction plan. &nbsp;The reductions were primarily in the United States and Europe. &nbsp;The Company incurred a pre-tax charge of approximately $1.6 million in connection with the reductions in workforce in the second quarter of 2005. &nbsp;In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, North America and South America, the charges incurred in the second quarter of 2005 were approximately $1.1 million, $392,000 and $97,000, respectively. &nbsp;Of this amount, approximately $537,000 was paid in the second quarter of 2005 and the remainder was paid in the third quarter of 2005. &nbsp;There were no amounts outstanding under this plan as of December 31, 2005.</P>

<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Note 18 &#150; Related party transactions</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Shared employees</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Certain of the Company&#146;s employees also perform services for unaffiliated companies owned by James R. Crane. &nbsp;The Company is reimbursed for these services based upon an allocation percentage of total salaries agreed to by the Company and Mr. Crane. &nbsp;The Company received reimbursements of $136,000, $135,000 and $62,000 for 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. &nbsp;Amounts billed but not received as of December 31, 2005 were $72,000 and are included in other receivables on the consolidated balance sheets.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Source One Spares</B></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Mr. Crane is a director and significant shareholder of Source One Spares, Inc. (&#147;Source One&#148;), a company specializing in the just-in-time delivery of overhauled components to commercial aircraft operators. &nbsp;During all periods presented, transactions with Source One were immaterial.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt"><B>Aircraft usage payments</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>During 2004 and 2003, the Company periodically utilized aircraft owned or leased by entities that are controlled by Mr. Crane. &nbsp;The Company was charged for actual usage of the aircraft on an hourly basis at market rates and was billed on a periodic basis. &nbsp;The Company reimbursed Mr. Crane for $1.2 million and $621,000 during 2004 and 2003, respectively, for actual hourly usage of the aircraft. &nbsp;In January 2005, the Company purchased from an unrelated third party an aircraft that was previously leased by an entity controlled by Mr. Crane for $12.5 million to be utilized for business travel, eliminating the use of Mr. Crane&#146;s aircraft and reimbursement thereof. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:0.05pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>On July 18, 2005, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company approved, in lieu of incremental cash compensation, an arrangement to provide Mr. Crane, or his designees, with up to an aggregate of 150 hours per year of personal use of the Company&#146;s aircraft without reimbursement by Mr. Crane. &nbsp;Mr. Crane actually used 158.7 hours in 2005. &nbsp;On March 15, 2006, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors approved the 8.7 hours of overage and reduced the amount allowed for personal usage in 2006 by 8.7 hours to 141.3 hours. &nbsp;The Company intends to include usage of 158.7 hours in Mr. Crane&#146;s taxable income as required by current U.S. federal income tax regulations. &nbsp;The U.S. federal income tax regulations also restrict the amount of corporate tax deductions for operating costs and tax depreciation attributable to personal use of the company plane. &nbsp;The amount of non-deductible personal use expense is reduced by the imputed income recognized by the employee. &nbsp;On August 5, 2005, the Board of Directors of the Company approved, in lieu of additional director cash compensation that would make the existing compensation package more competitive, an arrangement to provide the independent members of the Board of Directors with limited personal usage of the Company&#146;s aircraft, without reimbursement by the directors. &nbsp;Personal usage of the aircraft by the directors is subject to availability, with priority given to the Company&#146;s usage, and the cumulative number of hours allowed for all directors may not exceed 100 hours per year. &nbsp;The Company will record the number of hours utilized by each director and include in such director&#146;s yearly taxable income the amount required by then current U.S. federal income tax regulations. &nbsp;In 2005, the directors did not utilize the company plane.</P>

<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Revenues from transfers between divisions represent approximate amounts that would be charged if an unaffiliated company provided the services. &nbsp;Revenues and expenses for geographic divisions include 100 percent of amounts for unconsolidated affiliates directly involved in freight forwarding activities. &nbsp;Total divisional revenues are reconciled with total consolidated revenues by eliminating inter-divisional revenues and revenues and expenses for unconsolidated affiliates. &nbsp;Income (loss) before taxes includes profits (losses) on intercompany transactions. &nbsp;Net revenues by division for the year ended December 31, 2003 were restated in 2004 to exclude intercompany profits and losses. &nbsp;These reclassifications had no impact on consolidated net revenues.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:11pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>Performance measurement and resource allocation for the reportable segments are based on many factors. &nbsp;The primary financial measures used by management to evaluate the operating performance of the Company&#146;s segments include the revenues, costs and expenses directly controlled by each reportable segment and exclude the following: </P>

<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-54pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-13pt; padding-left:54pt; text-indent:-18pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>-</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:54pt; line-height:13pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify>interest and certain other miscellaneous nonoperating income and expenses not directly used in assessing the performance of the operating segments.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:11pt" align=justify><BR></P>
